subject: Lattice Health - ask to prioritize custom routing + audit export

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@latticehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Lattice Health - ask to prioritize custom routing + audit export

Team —

Quick context: Lattice Health (enterprise, ISV in healthcare) is at legal procurement. They asked for two blocking capabilities to close: 1) a tenant-aware custom routing rule so certain traffic can be pinned to a dedicated pool, and 2) a near-real-time audit export (S3 + secure transfer) for audit logs and model usage tied to their retention policy.

They've signaled willingness to commit to a 12-month Reserved Capacity if we can deliver a small scoped feature set as an activation condition. Sara is copied.

Asks:
- Irene / Product: can we scope a minimal MVP for routing + audit export that fits into a 6-8 week sprint? We want a clear list of acceptance criteria so Legal/Procurement can pick this up in SOW.
- Ben / Eng: rough feasibility and major risks (security, perf, SLO impact). If we can, can Eng propose a constrained technical approach (fallback behavior, config surface) that reduces productization effort?
- Monica / CS: advise on how urgent this is on their side and whether a staged delivery (routing first, audit second) would keep momentum.

Attachments: Lattice_SOW_Draft.pdf (customer redline), requested-routing-spec.md (customer scoping note)

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(415) 555-0126

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sara Holmes <sara.holmes@latticehealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Lattice Health - ask to prioritize custom routing + audit export

Thanks for the context, Jordan — copied Ben on the feasibility ask. A few high-level position notes from Product:

1) Routing MVP: we can probably ship a limited tenant-routing DSL that maps customer tenant IDs to a dedicated pool label (e.g., "dedicated-us-west-2-1") and a default fallback policy. Acceptance criteria we need: deterministic semantics, config persisted in control-plane, and runtime safe-fallback to shared pool when labeled pool is overloaded.

2) Audit export: we already have per-request telemetry; the gap is batching + secure export with per-tenant partitioning and retention controls. If we scope to a push-to-S3 mechanism (encrypted, per-tenant prefix) w/ delivery guarantees and retention metadata, that avoids building a new streaming infra.

Questions for scoping:
- Jordan/Monica: which data fields are non-negotiable for Lattice (PII redaction, per-token metadata)? The customer's draft SOW references per-request prompt+response hashes and token counts.
- Ben: can Eng implement tenant-routing as a policy layer in the control-plane with a runtime check? What's your estimate for a banded delivery (routing-only in 4 weeks, routing+export in 8)?

I'll assemble a proposed acceptance criteria doc and a rough roadmap entry for the next planning review.

Irene Choi
PM, Platform
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Lattice Health - ask to prioritize custom routing + audit export

Jordan / team —

From the customer's side: Sara confirmed this week that routing is the gating item; audit export is "highly desirable" but they view routing pinning as the procurement blocker. They are OK with a staged delivery where routing ships first and audit follows.

Operational asks from Lattice:
- They want per-tenant encryption keys (we can use CMK) and a retention window of 3 years for audit exports.
- They will need onboarding docs and a runbook for their SOC team.

One ask for Product: can we provide a provisional compatibility checklist so Legal can accept the SOW with a delivery milestone rather than a fully baked feature? Procurement is flexible if we show a concrete Milestone 1 definition.

I'll coordinate a technical demo next week with Sara if we have a short prototype.

—Monica

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Lattice Health - ask to prioritize custom routing + audit export

Short version: feasible with caveats.

Routing: implement as a control-plane policy that assigns a "pool_id" tag per-tenant. Runtime will consult pool_id and if labeled pool is healthy, route there; otherwise fallback to shared pool with an exponential backoff/bypass policy. Estimated effort: ~3.5 engineer-weeks to land a hardened control-plane config + 1.5 engineer-weeks to add safe runtime checks and monitoring. Ramp/QA time: 2 weeks. Total: ~7 weeks to ship routing MVP end-to-end.

Audit export: build a batcher that aggregates per-request telemetry into per-tenant parquet files and pushes to S3 with server-side encryption and a per-tenant prefix. Risk areas: the export path can add operational load; we'd need to cap export throughput or do sampled exports initially. Estimated baseline effort: ~4 engineer-weeks + 2 weeks QA/infra hardening. If we sample 10% of requests initially (configurable), we can reduce infra needs for the first delivery.

Given the estimates, a staged delivery makes sense: routing first (6-8 weeks), then audit export (additional 4-6 weeks depending on sampling). We can provide a provisional compatibility/acceptance checklist for Legal.

Next steps I propose:
- Product to publish acceptance criteria doc by EOD Friday.
- Eng to prepare a small scope PRD with the runtime fallback semantics and monitoring hooks.
- Jordan/Monica to confirm SOW milestone language and signoff window with the customer.

Happy to jump on a 30-min sync tomorrow to align on milestones.

Ben Carter
Engineering Manager, Runtime
ben.carter@redwood.com
